The client did not read this Arrow Flight SQL result for <timeout>; the query was cancelled. Read results without pausing, or raise "krishiv.flightSql.fetchIdleTimeout".

The Arrow Flight SQL <command> listing ran longer than its limit of <limit> and was stopped. Narrow its patterns, or raise "krishiv.flightSql.metadataTimeout".

This Arrow Flight SQL call needs a query, but the statement is not a query (its class is <statementClass>; it may have become a command through a changed ${...} variable). Nothing was run. Send it as a statement update (DoPut) or with GetFlightInfo of a new statement.
An Arrow Flight SQL update (DoPut) needs a statement that returns no rows, but this statement is a query. Nothing was run. Send it with GetFlightInfo and fetch its rows with DoGet.
The statement ran; its result (<size>) was not stored: <reason>. Do not run it again to see its effect; send a query to read the state it changed.
A result row of <columns> columns is larger than the <limit>-byte Arrow Flight SQL message limit and cannot be sent. Select fewer or smaller columns.
The result schema of this Arrow Flight SQL ticket changed since GetFlightInfo (a table it reads was altered). Call GetFlightInfo again for a new ticket.

The Arrow Flight SQL GetTables listing with table schemas matches <count> tables, over the limit of <limit>. Narrow the catalog, schema or table name pattern, or raise "krishiv.flightSql.maxSchemaTables".
The Arrow Flight SQL statement is <bytes> bytes long, over the limit of <limit> bytes. Shorten it, or raise "krishiv.flightSql.maxStatementBytes".

The write is not committed; <files>. Raising "commit.retry.num-retries" or "commit.retry.total-timeout-ms" on the table allows more attempts.

Please check to see whether or not your commit was successful before retrying this commit. Retrying an already successful operation will result in duplicate records or unintentional modifications.

The observation <name> was read before a DataFrame was observed with it. Call `DataFrame.observe` with it first. (PySpark's `NO_OBSERVE_BEFORE_GET`.)

Reading the file <path> failed: the object store did not complete the request after <attempts> attempt(s): <reason>. This is a storage failure, not a corrupt file, so it is never skipped by "ignoreCorruptFiles". Retry the query, or check the store's availability and permissions.
The observation <name> already observes a DataFrame: an Observation can be used with a DataFrame only once. (PySpark's `REUSE_OBSERVATION`.)

The Python data source <source> returned <bytes> bytes, over the <limit> byte limit of this embedded read path, which holds a source's rows in memory when a scan runs. Read less of it per query (narrow the source's options or split it into smaller sources).

The Python UDF <name>@<version> is registered with eval type <registered> but the plan calls it as <called> (eval type <evalType>): register the function on the executing session as the kind of call the query makes.

The Python UDF <name> returned a result that does not match what it declares: <reason>. Make the function return the declared columns, in their declared types, and for a grouped aggregate one value per group.
Python worker exited unexpectedly (crashed): <reason>. The next query starts a new worker. If a UDF ran out of memory, raise "krishiv.python.worker.memoryLimit".

<operation> needs <needed> Python UDF workers at once, and at most <available> can serve it: "<setting>" is <value>, and one of those workers is kept for scalar Python UDFs when there are 2 or more. Raise "<setting>", or call fewer Python UDFs in one operator.

The query was aborted to free memory for other work: it held <heldBytes> bytes, the most of any query, and spilling did not free enough memory in time. Increase "krishiv.memory.limit" or run fewer concurrent queries.
